description: Cosmic Explorers is a team passionate about space, astronomy, technology, and education. We aim to create an interactive space experience that helps people explore, learn, and have fun. We are looking for members interested in coding, AI, astronomy, design, education, and storytelling. Beginners and experienced participants are welcome.
summary:
VOIDQUEST: The Journey to Mars is an educational space adventure about what it really takes to live on another planet. You wake up aboard a spaceship bound for Mars, explore the ship, and learn real astronaut lessons. Then a solar flare hits and you race the clock to fix the engines and navigation. After landing in Jezero Crater, you build your base and have to survive: keep your sleep, hunger, thirst and sanity up by growing crops, recycling water, crafting food (coffee makes you faster!) and running daily checks on the solar panels, batteries, UV shields and oxygen filters.

Your real mission is science. Jump up rocky hills to collect samples, study them in the lab with a laser and spectrometer, and send the results back to Earth. Every rock unlocks a logbook page with real NASA facts. Ride out a dust storm, survive an oxygen emergency, and on your final day take the rover to a towering layered cliff to recover a mysterious sample that might change everything. Every fact in the game comes from NASA sources, and it plays on PC or on a phone.
details:
VOIDQUEST: The Journey to Mars is a browser game for children aged 7 to 12. Players follow a mission from Earth to Mars, and along the way they learn real space science through play rather than reading. Players complete challenges at each stage of the trip.

How it works: The game is split into quest stages, such as launch, travel through space and landing on Mars. Each stage teaches one real concept, like [gravity / orbits / the distance to Mars / conditions on the Martian surface], using short facts and challenges built into the gameplay.

Benefits and impact: Space science can feel abstract to young children. VOIDQUEST makes it hands-on and rewarding, so children remember what they learn because they used it to win. The game runs free in a web browser with no install, so any school, library or home with a computer can use it.

Tools and technologies: Godot, published on itch.io, Claude code for making audio sounds and images.

Creativity: Instead of a quiz with a spaceship theme, the learning is the game mechanic: players can only succeed by understanding the science.

What our team considered: Reading level and short attention spans for ages 7 to 12, simple controls, a game that works on low-spec school computers, and scientific accuracy
